The Nigerian Army has graduated 47 soldiers as military drivers after completing a basic driving course at the Headquarters 3 Division in Jos, Plateau State. The soldiers completed the Drivers Basic Course 2 of 2026, organised to improve their professional competence and strengthen the army’s operational mobility. The graduation ceremony was held at the 3 Division Auditorium, Maxwell Khobe Cantonment, Jos, with the General Officer Commanding 3 Division and Commander, Operation Enduring Peace, Major General W.M. Dangana, represented by the Commander, 53 Signals Brigade, Brigadier General P.A. Zipele. According to a statement issued on Friday by the Acting Deputy Director, Army Public Relations, 3 Division, Lieutenant Colonel Olumide Victor Olukoya, the GOC commended the Supply and Transport Drivers Training Wing for its commitment to developing competent military drivers. He emphasised the importance of transportation and logistics support to military operations, particularly in challenging terrains and demanding security environments. Charging the graduates to apply their training, the statement said, “Addressing the graduating soldiers, the GOC charged them to translate the knowledge and skills acquired during the course into practical performance in their respective units.” Army alerts Oyo residents as two-week military exercise begins Tuesday United Nigeria Airlines expands domestic flight routes Police storm Kogi forest, rescue 15 kidnap victims It further stated that they were expected to demonstrate discipline, vigilance, responsibility and professionalism in their duties. The statement added, “Safe driving practices and proper vehicle handling are essential to the protection of lives, military equipment and the successful execution of assigned missions.” Earlier, the Commander, 73 Supply and Transport Brigade, Colonel O.C. Okungbure, described the graduation as another milestone in the division’s efforts to develop a skilled and professional workforce. He said the training covered military driving procedures, traffic laws and safety precautions. The statement read, “The course provided the 47 participants with essential driving competencies, including adherence to military driving procedures, traffic laws and safety precautions.” It added that the training would “enhance operational mobility, improve logistics support and facilitate the effective movement of troops and equipment in both routine and operational environments.” Okungbure urged the graduates to uphold the standards acquired during the course and remain worthy ambassadors of the Nigerian Army in their respective formations and units. The ceremony featured a review of the course activities, presentation of certificates, and group photographs.
